milestones.title: Foundation and discovery
milestones.delivered: Original articles, six topics, search, reading lists and a selected timeline.
milestones.next: Continue to maintain links, accessibility and source attribution.

milestones.title: Unified site-wide navigation
milestones.delivered: Explore, Scripture, Research and Project menus expose every major public hub on desktop and mobile. Source/accessibility audit is exposed under Research; disclosure-group scripting now handles the whole menu collection and closes on focus leaving a group. October 2026 usability revision: split the expanding Research menu into three labelled desktop columns of five, four and four links, Explore into two columns of four and three, and retained native, stacked disclosure sections for touch/mobile use. Desktop fine-pointer menus now open on hover and close when the pointer leaves both trigger and descendant panel, while keyboard focus, Escape, click-outside, active-route indication and mobile tap toggles remain supported. Added a no-gap pointer transition, compact responsive columns, height-constrained overflow on short desktop viewports, and explicit whole-site nav coverage tests. This navigation revision was merged as GitHub PR #31 (commit 3806f740a559de78318466e988aff139160ff120) following successful root and subpath CI validation; the public release register now records it. Explore's Culture and language column now presents a direct reading route to Chaldean ecclesiastical naming and shared Assyrian heritage, balanced at four items in each Explore column.
milestones.next: Run manual real-device keyboard/screen-reader, large zoom, mobile landscape and Mac Safari hover/focus testing, including diagonal movement into Research's three columns. Automated coverage verifies markup and source guardrails, not actual assistive technology behaviour.

milestones.title: Biblical primary-text collection
milestones.delivered: Local Bible reader, named-reference index and 26 original guides with explicit passage references.
milestones.next: Add careful textual comparison and qualified specialist review where applicable.

milestones.title: Encyclopaedia expansion and preservation
milestones.delivered: Expanded the original collection with 14 specialist-sourced, independently authored historical guides covering eight rulers, governance, deportation, religion, languages, the imperial collapse and later regional history. Added 56 section-level reading trails, 10 source records and dated timeline routes. Earlier preserved reference corpus, glossary and measured growth dashboard remain available. Added another eight original language and heritage studies without importing unlicensed texts. Six further original methods and community-heritage studies now complement ancient history and linguistic resources. Milestone 9 adds eight long-form Bible-primary, object-identified comparisons (40 precisely mapped new sections), six curated specialist and museum reference records and a public evidence dossier reading hub. The release also connects the new studies to older Bible and history entries. Nine additional Middle Assyrian social-history guides provide 45 sourced sections and a period-sensitive non-royal reading pathway. Nine original accession-level tablet and archaeological object case files add 36 linked research sections with explicit physical source identifiers. A new five-section guide teaches cuneiform sign transliteration, normalized Akkadian and source-critical translation uncertainty.
milestones.next: Continue original-language and household records, while independently checking Church of the East and Chaldean naming sources. Expand evidence-based Assyrian heritage across denominations without confusing ancient Kaldu, Syriac language classification or church membership with a universal modern identity assignment.

milestones.title: The Middle Assyrian world and everyday life
milestones.delivered: Published nine original source-mapped guides with 45 substantive editorial sections about Middle Assyrian provincial administration, law, women, households, fields, irrigation, livestock, dependent labour, ration lists, scribal archives, sealings, religion and exchange. Added ten externally attributed specialist source records, fourteen anchored claim reviews, a public research hub, reciprocal reading routes and a non-royal timeline entry. Legal prescriptions are distinguished from practice; Old and Neo-Assyrian and biblical comparisons are explicitly dated and limited. Follow-up object cases now connect social-history claims to seven dated or period-assigned Oracc tablet editions and a seal-impressed museum object.
milestones.next: Extend from introductory object dossiers to named and dated legal, women, family, agricultural and temple cases with exact line collations and qualified Assyriological and palaeographic review.

milestones.title: Individual tablet studies and archaeological case files
milestones.delivered: Published nine original, individually identified object studies with 36 separate section-to-source evidence trails. Eight are Middle Assyrian tablets or a seal-impressed museum object, and one later Babylonian Chronicle is explicitly separate. Each study displays accession or CDLI/edition IDs, provenance or acknowledged missing findspot, chronology, source-document type, relevant edited line scope and an external institutional record. Eight new source records and twelve anchored review claims accompany a browsable /case-files/ hub, a public JSON catalogue and automated metadata, accessibility and deployment checks. A follow-up transliteration layer now provides 16 short cited source-text lines with original editorial glosses for seven edited tablets; two other objects remain explicitly edition-pending. A curated concordance now connects named object catalogues and exact edited lines to terms, other research articles and separate biblical accounts.
milestones.next: Continue individual specialist edition and findspot verification and extend object-level indexing only when terms and manuscript contexts are independently checked.

milestones.title: Ancient texts and translation comparisons
milestones.delivered: Published a side-by-side ancient-text reading room and embedded comparison panels on all nine archaeological object articles. Sixteen very short credited sign-sequence excerpts from seven ATMAP/TCMA Middle Assyrian edited tablets include line identifiers, editorial English reading cues, source interpretive limits and visible damaged, restored or queried notation. Two catalogue-only objects have no invented transliteration or translation. Added one five-section methodological article with precise section evidence links, three new technical and scholarly source references, nine additional anchored claim-review records, a public comparison JSON export and negative tests that reject missing credit, false periods and fabricated unverified text. Follow-up concordance links now target stable identifiers for the sixteen short credited transliteration lines, with document-level fallback where no line edition exists.
milestones.next: Commission independent collation of the cited line readings, support documented alternative readings and maintain consistent term disambiguation between ancient sources.

milestones.title: Ancient text concordance and cross-reference index
milestones.delivered: Published a locally compiled, search-and-filter accessible concordance of 25 manually curated people, place, materials, institutions and text-method entries. It includes 32 documented object-level or edition-specific cross-references, 43 reading routes into existing encyclopaedia chapters, and 11 Bible comparison routes with deliberate genre/period separation. Edited text references deep-link directly to unique quotation-line IDs; object-only catalogue evidence is kept distinct. Reciprocal links appear on relevant editorial article pages, and an offline JSON export, regression tests, accessible search controls, main navigation links and live deployment checks are implemented. No extra original article or external source records are claimed.
milestones.next: Use the new evidence-limited name and identity register to guide source-checked editorial links. Extend term coverage only after independent specialists verify original names and disambiguation evidence.

milestones.title: Ancient names and historical identity disambiguation
milestones.delivered: Published eight individual name and place dossiers with twelve source-scoped object and biblical reading routes. Each records exact concordance anchors, name forms, what its current evidence does and does not establish, and checks needed before any historical identity claim. Added a public page and JSON export, Research navigation and concordance links, reusable validation and regression tests. The records are editorial, not independently specialist-reviewed, and they add no invented cuneiform signs, original manuscripts or new archaeological identities.
milestones.next: Commission Assyriological and biblical specialist review of original-language names, surviving editions, physical objects, chronology and location evidence. Require exact new accession or inscription line references and recorded reviewer assessment before asserting same-person or same-place identifications.

milestones.title: Chaldean Catholic affiliation and shared Assyrian heritage - source-critical identity history
milestones.delivered: Expanded and independently re-sourced the Assyrian identity, Syriac Christian traditions and Chaldean Catholic Church articles, and added a ten-section Chaldean naming and Assyrian heritage guide exposed under Explore. The archive states clearly that Catholic religious communion and a church title alone cannot establish an ancient separate ethnicity or language; it documents common East Syriac and Assyrian heritage, distinguishes the ancient Babylonian Kaldu from modern church terminology, identifies Chaldean church-label use in 1445 and Catholic developments in the sixteenth century, and corrects the false implication that modern ethnic applications were invented only in the late 1990s. It documents Assyrian cross-denominational advocacy and differing contemporary individual ethnic self-identification without imposing a label on every person. Seven new independent/institutional specialist source records bring the curated source library from 131 to 138, first-party Chaldean Catholic sources now disclose that they are not independent authorities on ethnicity, source trails for four identity-related articles cover 29 sections including the retained legacy naming paragraph and bring total mapped sections to 376, and eight additional pending claims CL-081 to CL-088 bring the anchored review register to 88. CI now checks source identities, institutional role caveats, ancient-modern category limits and navigation. This source correction and new guide were merged as PR #33 at commit 0703307fc5a8f4cab13cd4ef6464acafb09643bf, after passing all research source tests and full root and Pages project-path validation. The public revision ledger records this release as REV-0018.
milestones.next: Independently verify the original 1445 papal brief and relevant sixteenth-century records rather than relying only on specialist summaries. Document the original Raphael Bidawid interview if available, assess the GEDSH and academic interpretations through named Syriac and Assyriological reviewers, and seek first-hand oral histories across Assyrian and Chaldean Catholic families. Maintain transparent church institutional vs independent scholarly source roles; never infer malign intent or modern ethnicity from religious affiliation alone. Extend ancient Assyrian identity and continuity coverage by individually cited documentary and linguistic evidence.

milestones.title: Royal inscriptions and biblical cross-verification
milestones.delivered: Introduced a source-scoped research room with six side-by-side comparisons covering Shalmaneser III and Jehu, Sargon II and Ashdod, Sennacherib's Judah campaign, Jerusalem, tribute quantities and the distinct Lachish palace relief. Five cases identify exact ORACC royal edition coordinates (Q004693, Q006488 and Q003496); the sixth retains British Museum object 124904 as visual evidence, not invented cuneiform text. Three new primary edition source records and ten validated biblical reading routes are documented. Explicitly retains the 800 versus 300 silver talent disagreement and independently reviewed status remains pending. Includes offline JSON, reciprocal encyclopaedia links, Research navigation, CI negative tests and generated-link checks. Four directly anchored claim review records and four new source mappings in existing historical guides link each named royal edition to exact article-level arguments, bringing the total pending claim review register to 66. This feature was merged as PR #29 after root and GitHub Pages subpath validation; the public release ledger records the actual immutable merge SHA.
milestones.next: Obtain independent Assyriological, biblical and chronological review of all six original royal comparisons. The separately released Samaria succession room now covers Tiglath-pileser III, Shalmaneser V and Sargon II. Further expansion to Esarhaddon, the fall of Nineveh and other new editions must retain exact source identifiers and no invented harmonisation.

milestones.title: The Fall of Samaria and Assyrian succession
milestones.delivered: Published a dedicated four-phase research room following Menahem, northern annexations, the broken Pekah-Hoshea succession account, Shalmaneser V's siege setting, competing Sargon II conquest claims, royal deportation totals and variants, and later provincial resettlement. Eight separately scoped comparisons cite five exact RINAP 1/2 royal editions plus a clearly labelled specialist synthesis, with twelve biblical reading routes, direct edition locations, restored-sign and chronographic limitations. The dataset has an offline JSON export, accessible progressive phase filtering, Research navigation, reciprocal encyclopedia dossier links, and a six-section expansion of the existing Samaria study with six anchored claim-level checks. A dedicated negative-test suite covers fabricated lines, swapped Bible ranges and false royal attribution. Maintained sources expanded from 119 to 124 and the pending claim review register from 66 to 72. The feature was merged as PR #30 at commit c2d15f93edbe3d99e167351271103174c15d560e after successful CI root and project-path builds; the public revision ledger now records its immutable source.
milestones.next: Commission independent Assyriological review of RINAP 1 Q003455 damaged Pekah/Hoshea verb and the Q006488/Q006555 Samarian deportation numerical variants, with exemplar-by-exemplar collation and alternative readings. Evaluate the Babylonian Chronicle references to Shalmaneser V without equating same-sounding towns; obtain biblical chronological review of 2 Kings 17-18. Only after review consider qualified atlas province boundaries and detailed historical date bands. The new exile/provinces reading room further anchors a Samaria administrative letter outside royal victory rhetoric.

milestones.title: Exile, resettlement and life in Assyrian provinces
milestones.delivered: A new source-typed research room examines twelve separate comparisons across northern deportation, biblical destinations Halah, Gozan-Habor and the Medes, Sargonic resettlement and named new settlers, an original Neo-Assyrian Samarian corn-tax letter SAA 1 220 / P334789, separately identified Aramaean logistics and marriage correspondence SAA 19 17-18, two distinct museum reliefs, and provincial archaeological interpretation. Includes seventeen precise Bible reading routes, thirteen cross-linked source records and a five-category accessible filter, machine-readable local JSON and reciprocal article links. The existing Assyrian deportation dossier gained seven newly written substantial sections and the Samaria dossier an additional non-royal archival case study, adding eight mapped evidence trails. Seven new individual institutional or academic records increased the curated source library from 124 to 131; eight text-anchored claims CL-073 to CL-080 brought the pending-review queue to 80. Source roles and limitations are encoded and regression-tested; categories and menu lengths are rebalanced. User-device and independent expert review remain open. The release merged as PR #32 at commit 424e0db538d6dbca808ff795a14260291c0f4cc9 after passing all unit/invariant tests and full root and Pages-subpath validation. Its original merge is recorded as REV-0017.
milestones.next: Secure Assyriological line review of SAA 01 220 (P334789) and directly trace SAA 19 17, SAA 19 18 and SAA 16 63 to the original surviving tablets and verified signs. Commission a historical-geographical review of Halah-Halahhu, Guzana, Habor, Median destinations and their chronological assumptions before plotting any migration route. Review Oxford and Cambridge provincial archaeology in full and resolve image rights before expanding museum illustrations. Pursue provincial letters and household records without equating name forms, modern identities, and deportee ancestry.

milestones.title: Interactive historical atlas
milestones.delivered: The interactive historical atlas has eleven dated teaching stages with preserved offline basemap data, timeline playback, modern geography and city context. Milestone 3 adds chapter-specific reconstruction limits, source-by-source scope notes, clearer differentiation of provincial control from vassalage or temporary military reach, 21 linked historical and biblical reading routes, and checks that keep map citations and article links current.
milestones.next: Continue specialist cartographic and historical review before refining polygon coordinates. Map individual provinces only when dated inscriptional, administrative and archaeological evidence supports them. Test real browser behaviour, reduced-motion support and mobile readability. No numerical border certainty or ancient area estimates are justified.

milestones.title: Section-level source traceability
milestones.delivered: Evidence Register, source-to-guide links and 376 section-level evidence trails across 96 editorial guides, including 24 new heritage and community research sections. Added 32 curated object and edited-line concordance relationships, 43 chapter links and 11 separately labelled Scripture comparisons; these are indexed connections rather than new section-level evidence trails.
milestones.next: Extend term-level and passage-level verification with qualified specialists, preserving documented edited-line identity and the distinction between lexical similarities and historical equivalence. Maintain a source-role audit of church institutional claims used in contested Assyrian/Chaldean identity sections.

milestones.title: Historical claim verification
milestones.delivered: The claim-level review register now contains 88 text-anchored records, including seventy-three newer biblical, inscriptional and edition-method records, with nine additional transliteration and uncertainty checks linked to named texts. Passage coordinates, direct-vs-context source roles and review limitations are validated; no independent specialist reviews have been claimed.
milestones.next: Prioritise independent review of the direct royal inscription comparisons and existing 88 claim reviews; checks of ORACC IDs, edition coordinates and local Bible passages establish traceability, not historical agreement.

milestones.title: Assyrian languages and cultural heritage
milestones.delivered: Added eight original specialist-sourced guides with 32 section reading trails on cuneiform interpretation, Syriac manuscript hands and Unicode, local NENA dialects, Urmi documentation, Surayt and ethical recording. A new navigable language reference room presents 22 Unicode-identified Syriac letters, links to HMML manuscript lessons and Cambridge field recordings for Urmi, Alqosh and Ankawa. No third-party audio or protected manuscript images are copied. A new original reading-method guide and linked short transliteration comparisons make editorial sign notation and damage/restoration distinctions explicit.
milestones.next: Get an Assyriologist to review original Akkadian notation in all seven excerpted editions. Add additional original-language documentation without falsely presenting a Syriac translation of a cuneiform tablet.

milestones.title: Community testimony and heritage media
milestones.delivered: Launched a public heritage and oral-history reference room containing ten previously published, externally linked records across migration, community institutions, cultural practice and living speech. Added six original method and history guides with 24 source-mapped sections, three blank downloadable planning worksheets, a locally filtered source index and explicit rights, narrator consent and privacy safeguards. No family submissions or protected recordings have been collected or published.
milestones.next: Establish a separately authorised custodian, secure intake and informed-consent review process before collecting personal testimony. Invite community and subject specialists, document narrator review and access restrictions, and add village-specific sourced entries and permission-cleared media only after the needed agreements exist.

milestones.title: Secure contribution delivery
milestones.delivered: Dormant backend is retained and public contributions remain download-only.
milestones.next: Do not imply a working private corrections inbox or media-intake workflow. Authorise a protected, staffed delivery service before taking personal reports, promising responses or storing consent records.

milestones.title: Editorial governance and revision history
milestones.delivered: Published a public editorial governance and revision room, correction/clarification/withdrawal policy, defined role disclosures, two blank release and correction planning documents, and a validated register of eighteen merged major milestones (including governance, stewardship, source/accessibility, historical evidence, Middle Assyrian life, object case files, original-language comparisons and the source concordance, name disambiguation original royal source comparisons and the fall of Samaria succession dossier) with their actual merged commits and pull request links. No independent reviewers have been assigned or claimed, and no confirmed public correction notices have been fabricated. Existing article and local correction-draft flows now link to the policy.
milestones.next: Record substantive merged content releases and any documented corrections against actual GitHub merges. Obtain named independent review of inscription readings and Bible comparisons, and complete human accessibility review before publication-readiness claims.

milestones.title: Source integrity and accessibility audit
milestones.delivered: Added an offline structural audit for the maintained curated institutional source URLs, a separate bounded monthly/manual HTTP health workflow with inconclusive 403/429/timeout handling, a public audit and metadata report, representative-page accessibility markup checks, and automated test coverage. Repaired multi-menu keyboard disclosure handling, improved focus and reduced-motion CSS, and introduced nonvisual atlas chapter status announcements. These checks do not claim real browser testing, all-source remote verification or full WCAG conformance.
milestones.next: Run and manually assess the scheduled URL-health observations for the expanded 113-record curated source registry, then test screen readers and zoom on the new case-file provenance panels. Retain indexing as blocked on human approvals.

milestones.title: Publication and long-term stewardship
milestones.delivered: Added a dedicated public publication and preservation room, deterministic SHA-256 fixity manifest covering generated files, strict missing/extra/tampered-file verification, recoverable deterministic ZIP export with tested extraction, CI negative tests and restore checks for build and Pages deployment, plus selected live-file hash probes and an operational recovery runbook. Existing noindex safeguards remain unchanged.
milestones.next: Assign a backup custodian and establish independent offsite copies and restoration drills. Use the new source and accessibility audit procedures to review remote citations and real-device WCAG 2.2 usability before any indexing approval. Rights, specialist historical/linguistic review and live publisher availability still require human checks.
